items.followUp: Name and briefly explain any four types of software piracy.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies softlifting and relates it to unauthorised copying or licence violation.
rubric.description: Softlifting is making or installing extra software copies in violation of the licence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming softlifting and explaining that it involves unauthorised copies or use beyond the licence.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies client-server overuse and explains that network use exceeds the licence limit.
rubric.description: Client-server overuse allows more users to access network software than the licence permits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this type and describing use by more users than the licence allows.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies hard-disk loading and describes the unauthorised preinstallation of software.
rubric.description: Hard-disk loading is when a seller installs unauthorised software on a computer before selling it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this type and explaining that a seller preinstalls unauthorised software.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies counterfeiting and explains that unauthorised copies are made to resemble genuine software.
rubric.description: Software counterfeiting is making and selling unauthorised copies that imitate genuine software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this type and describing the making or selling of fake copies.

modelAnswer: Softlifting: making or installing extra copies of software in violation of its licence.
Client-server overuse: allowing more users to access network software than the licence permits.
Hard-disk loading: a computer seller installs unauthorised software on a computer before selling it.
Software counterfeiting: making and selling unauthorised copies that imitate genuine software.
